## Affordable Costa Rica in 7 days: what the itinerary includes

**Travelers choose this tour to explore several outstanding natural regions in just one week.** Over 7 days and 6 nights, guests travel via [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/), head to the canals of [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), continue to [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), and finish at [Manuel Antonio National Park](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/) on the Pacific coast.

The name “Affordable Costa Rica” refers to a particular tour; it does not, by itself, mean that every expense is covered. The package includes transportation, accommodation, excursions with an English-speaking guide, specified entrance tickets, and meals on the scheduled days. Admission to Tortuguero National Park, certain fees, optional activities, and personal expenses are paid separately. These inclusions and exclusions matter when comparing prices.

## The week at a glance: when to expect early starts

| Day | Plan |
|---|---|
| 1 | Arrival in San José |
| 2 | Overland transfer and boat to Tortuguero |
| 3 | Morning in Tortuguero, transfer to Arenal |
| 4 | Mistico bridges and volcanic trails |
| 5 | Transfer to Manuel Antonio |
| 6 | National park walk and beach |
| 7 | Return to the airport |

On day two, departure from San José is scheduled for around 6:00 a.m. The route passes through [Braulio Carrillo](/costa-rica/place/braulio-carrillo-national-park/) and continues to the Caño Blanco dock, where the boat journey begins. A breakfast stop is planned along the way. After arrival, guests explore Tortuguero village and its turtle museum.

An early excursion is scheduled for the morning of day three, at approximately 6:15 a.m. The journey then continues north toward Arenal, where hot springs are on the itinerary. This is a fairly full schedule: during the first 3 days you cross from the capital to the Caribbean side of Costa Rica and travel back inland to the volcanic region.

## Tortuguero: boating and wildlife watching

[Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/) is known for its waterways, birds, humid tropical forest, and protected natural environment. The tour includes a boat transfer and an early-morning nature excursion. Sightings of particular animals cannot be guaranteed: their presence and visibility depend on local conditions.

If sea turtles are your main reason for visiting, check the season and the regulated arrangements for viewing them separately. Nighttime observations on the beach are governed by SINAC rules and are not automatically included in every tour stopping in Tortuguero.

**Entrance to Tortuguero National Park is paid separately**, even though other admission tickets are included in the package. Remember this when calculating the overall budget.

## Arenal: suspension bridges and ancient lava flows

Day four takes place in the [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) area. At Mistico Park, guests walk forest trails and suspension bridges. The approximately 2-mile route takes around 2.5 hours and includes 15 bridges, 6 of them hanging bridges. An afternoon excursion explores volcanic terrain transformed by the 1968 eruption.

These are guided nature walks, not technical mountaineering on the volcano. Trails can be wet, so closed-toe shoes, a lightweight rain jacket, and drinking water are useful. Views of the summit depend on cloud cover.

## Monteverde and Manuel Antonio: what is actually included

[Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) is mentioned in the route on day five, but the day's description specifies **a transfer to Manuel Antonio** and free time after arrival. Do not assume this seven-day tour includes a separate, substantial visit to the Monteverde reserve: no such excursion is described for that day.

Day six is devoted to [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/). A trail through the tropical forest leads to a beach, with an approximately 20-minute stop planned. Birds, sloths, monkeys, and other wildlife may be seen along the way, but no individual sighting is guaranteed. **This is an excursion with a short beach visit, not a multi-day beach holiday.**

For a longer stay by the ocean, consider the [10-day tour via Arenal to the Pacific beaches](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-3-perspectives/). The [14-day “Best of Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/best-of-costa-rica/) also includes Corcovado, Caño Island, and additional natural areas in the south.

## What to consider before choosing and paying

The tour lasts 7 days and 6 nights, with prices starting at $2081. Before deciding, compare that price with the accommodation, meal arrangements, group excursion format, and separately charged items. Breakfasts, lunches, and dinners are included on different days rather than uniformly throughout the itinerary; check the daily schedule instead of assuming three meals every day.

Seasonal weather also varies by region. The Caribbean coast around Tortuguero has no single clearly defined dry season, while the Pacific coast generally experiences a drier period from December through March. Waterproof items and footwear suitable for forest trails and boarding boats are helpful on this trip.

To compare more wildlife-focused options, explore [Costa Rica nature tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/costa-rica/) or the [full tour catalog](/costa-rica/tour/). Compare the number of days spent in parks and the time spent traveling, rather than just the advertised duration.

## Frequently asked questions about the affordable tour

### Are there free days to spend at the beach?

There is no extended beach segment. Day six includes a walk through Manuel Antonio with a short stop on the shore. Choose another itinerary if you want several full days by the ocean.

### Can we see turtles in Tortuguero?

Tortuguero is known for protecting sea turtles, but nesting excursions, the season, and the relevant permits need to be confirmed separately. Standard river excursions do not guarantee turtle sightings.

### Are all national park admission fees included?

No. Admission to Tortuguero is specifically listed as an extra charge. Other entrance tickets are included among the services covered by the tour.

## Classic Costa Rica: coffee, volcanoes, and cloud forests in 6 days

**6 days and 5 nights** in central Costa Rica offer volcanic scenery, an insight into coffee production, and two distinct natural ecosystems. The journey begins in [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/), takes in the [Arenal Volcano region](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), and explores [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) before returning to the capital.

This itinerary suits travelers seeking a busy nature-focused holiday with organized transfers and guided excursions. There is no beach portion: all six days revolve around coffee, volcanoes, waterfalls, wildlife, and mountain forests.

## Day two: a coffee estate, the Poás crater, and La Paz Waterfalls

After the first night in San José, the route begins at [Doka Coffee Estate](/costa-rica/place/doka-estate/). During the visit, you learn how coffee beans are cultivated, processed, and roasted. This is a substantial part of the itinerary, linking the tour to both [Costa Rica's natural attractions](/interests/wildlife/tours/costa-rica/) and [coffee-focused travel](/interests/coffee-tours/).

Next comes [Poás Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/), known for its crater and volcanic activity. Access to viewpoints depends on current conservation rules and weather conditions: visibility and the availability of a particular viewing area cannot be guaranteed in advance.

The third stop of the day is [La Paz Waterfalls](/costa-rica/place/la-paz-waterfalls/). Here guests explore waterfalls, forest paths, and nature exhibits, including areas devoted to birds and butterflies. Afterward, the itinerary continues toward Arenal, with the night scheduled at **Arenal Paraíso Resort & Spa**.

This is the busiest day of the trip, combining three different attractions with an interregional transfer. If you would like more time at the coffee estate or volcano, the schedule must be adjusted to accommodate the day's overall travel time.

## Caño Negro: wildlife watching from a boat

Day three focuses on [Caño Negro Wildlife Refuge](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/). The main activity is a boat trip to observe riverside vegetation, birds, and other wildlife. Monkeys, caimans, sloths, and basilisks are among the animals mentioned in descriptions of the region.

**Wildlife sightings depend on natural conditions.** Even when a species lives in the refuge, its appearance on a given excursion is never guaranteed. What distinguishes Caño Negro is that visitors mostly observe the wildlife from the water rather than on forest trails.

After the boat excursion and lunch, you return to Arenal. This is the second night at Arenal Paraíso Resort & Spa, so there is no need to change hotels immediately after the excursion.

## Lake Arenal and a canopy adventure above Monteverde's forest

On day four, travelers cross [Lake Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) by boat toward Monteverde. Both the climate and the forest change here: cloud forests at altitude are often wrapped in mist and have high humidity.

The highlight of day four is **a canopy tour above the tropical treetops**. Participants must follow the operator's instructions and account for any age, weight, or health restrictions. Exact participation requirements should be confirmed before booking. Resplendent quetzals and other birds live in this area, but sightings of any particular species are not guaranteed.

Accommodation is arranged at **El Establo Mountain Resort**. Day five is devoted to the [Monteverde cloud forest](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), with nature walks and opportunities to observe plants and birds. At this elevation, conditions may be cool and damp even when San José is warm.

| Day | Main destination |
|---|---|
| 1 | Arrival in San José |
| 2 | Doka, Poás, La Paz |
| 3 | Caño Negro Wildlife Refuge |
| 4 | Lake Arenal and canopy tour |
| 5 | Monteverde cloud forest |
| 6 | Return to San José |

## Hotels, guides, and included services

The itinerary includes the first night at **Barceló San Jose Palacio**, followed by two nights at **Arenal Paraíso Resort & Spa** and two nights at **El Establo Mountain Resort**. Day six ends with a transfer to San José International Airport.

The tour includes **transportation and transfers, accommodation, local taxes, entrance tickets, an English-speaking guide during excursions, and meals as specified in the itinerary**. Optional tours, certain arrival and departure taxes, and personal hotel expenses are extra.

Because the route passes through several climate zones, pack shoes suitable for damp trails, a rain jacket, and warmer clothing for Monteverde. The word “Spa” in the name of the Arenal hotel does not mean that separate spa treatments are included.

## Who is this classic itinerary for, and what can you compare it with?

Travelers choose this tour to see a coffee estate, an active volcano, water-based wildlife reserves, and a cloud forest within a short period, without extensive self-driving. If [coffee farms](/interests/coffee-tours/) are your main interest, the visit to Doka is particularly appealing. Bird enthusiasts will enjoy the opportunities at Caño Negro and Monteverde.

To finish with beach time and travel by car, compare it with the [11-day itinerary via Tortuguero and Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-self-drive-2024/). Note that the name of that itinerary includes the year 2024. For southern rainforest and Pacific reefs, there is a [five-day Corcovado and Caño Island program](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-san-jose-treasures/). Find more options in the [Costa Rica tour catalog](/costa-rica/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about Classic Costa Rica

### Is the coffee plantation excursion included?

Yes. Day two includes a visit to [Doka Estate](/costa-rica/place/doka-estate/) to learn about coffee production, followed by Poás Volcano and La Paz Waterfalls.

### Is a view of the Poás crater guaranteed?

No. Visibility and access to a particular viewing platform depend on weather, volcanic activity, and conservation authority rules.

### Do I need to rent a car myself?

No. The confirmed inclusions specify organized transportation and transfers. Renting a vehicle is not the main travel arrangement on this tour.

### Are there free days on the beach?

No. The itinerary concentrates on inland Costa Rica: coffee, volcanoes, wildlife reserves, and cloud forests.

## “3 Perspectives on Costa Rica”: 10 days between volcanoes and the ocean

The [“3 Perspectives on Costa Rica” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-3-perspectives/) brings three experiences together: an introduction in [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/), a lively program of volcanic and forest excursions, and an extended stay on the [Pacific coast](/costa-rica/place/pacific-coast/). The total duration is **10 days and 9 nights**.

The tour is especially suitable for travelers eager to discover Costa Rica's natural landscapes without spending every day on the road or hiking. The first three days introduce several of the country's best-known natural regions, after which the itinerary becomes a beach holiday.

## Coffee, Poás, and La Paz Waterfalls in one excursion day

After arrival and the first night in San José comes the most varied day of the itinerary. It starts at [Doka Coffee Estate](/costa-rica/place/doka-estate/), where you learn about growing, processing, and roasting coffee beans. For anyone particularly interested in coffee culture, this is a substantial themed experience, although the tour as a whole goes well beyond [coffee-focused journeys](/interests/coffee-tours/).

The route then ascends to [Poás Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/). The experience here depends on volcanic activity, cloud cover, and current national park restrictions. The volcano is at altitude, so the air can feel considerably cooler than in the warm lowlands. The park has its own entry and advance-booking rules; check the precise requirements before traveling.

The next stop is [La Paz Waterfalls](/costa-rica/place/la-paz-waterfalls/), where walks along forest paths combine with opportunities to see distinctive tropical wildlife. Three different experiences are scheduled on the same day, so the time at each is limited. This is an introduction to the sites rather than a multi-day exploration of each one.

## Arenal: two days among forests and traces of eruptions

The next natural region is [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/). The itinerary includes a walk across suspension bridges in the tropical forest and a hike in the national park, including terrain covered with volcanic rocks. Views of the summit depend on cloud cover; coming solely for a guaranteed panorama would be a mistake.

Walking the official trails does not mean climbing the active volcanic cone. Visitors can use designated paths and viewpoints. Closed-toe footwear, rain protection, and readiness for humid weather are important. Check the difficulty and duration of the chosen trail against your group's fitness level.

For a longer and more active nature-focused segment, compare this route with the [“5 Wonders of Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-wonders/), which adds Río Celeste, Monteverde, and canopy activities to the volcanic regions.

## Why the beach portion takes up most of the trip

Day four includes the transfer to the ocean. Days 5–9 are primarily free time on the [Pacific coast](/costa-rica/place/pacific-coast/). After the active days around the volcanoes, you can decide how to spend your time: on the beach, exploring the shoreline, relaxing at your hotel, or enjoying optional activities.

This balance appeals to travelers who want both excursions and a conventional vacation. The trade-off is straightforward: over 10 days, this route covers fewer natural regions than a busy circuit but provides considerably more free time by the sea.

| Stage of the tour | Main purpose |
|---|---|
| San José | Arrival and beginning of the route |
| Poás, Doka, La Paz | Coffee, volcano, and waterfalls |
| Arenal | Forest trails and volcano |
| Pacific coast | Several free days |

The last day has two possible endings: continuing your beach vacation or returning to the airport. When arranging international flights, choose and confirm the desired option rather than assuming both alternatives are included at once.

## Services, meals, and what to pack

The trip includes accommodation in the hotels specified by the itinerary, transfers, scheduled excursions, the services of a Russian-speaking guide, and accommodation taxes. Meals vary by day, with breakfasts included during the beach portion. Additional activities, airport fees, and personal expenses are paid separately.

Weather conditions differ along the route. Light warm and waterproof clothing is useful in the high-altitude areas of Poás and Arenal; on the coast, bring sun protection and swimwear. Brief tropical showers are possible even during periods generally considered drier.

Before booking, compare [other Costa Rica tours](/costa-rica/tour/) by the length of their beach stays. If birds, humid forests, and diverse national parks are your priorities, also browse [nature-focused journeys](/interests/wildlife/).

## Frequently asked questions about “3 Perspectives on Costa Rica”

### How many days are available for relaxing by the ocean?

The transfer to the coast is on day four, and days 5–9 are free for a beach holiday. Day ten depends on the selected ending of the itinerary.

### Is there a Russian-speaking guide?

Yes. A Russian-speaking guide is listed among the included services.

### Is the coffee estate visit included?

Yes. The visit to Doka is part of the excursion day with Poás Volcano and La Paz Waterfalls.

### Is this tour suitable for serious trekking?

There are forest walks and hikes in Arenal National Park, but no multi-day sporting trek. For a more active option, compare the [“5 Wonders of Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-wonders/).

## Costa Rica in 5 days: Tortuguero's canals, Poás Volcano, and La Paz Waterfalls

This route is intended for travelers who want to experience Costa Rica's natural diversity in just a few days without completing a long circuit around the country. You begin and end the journey in [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/), spend **two nights in Tortuguero**, explore tropical forests by boat, and return to the capital region on a small aircraft. The final excursion-packed day focuses on a volcano and waterfalls.

Unlike an itinerary with two days of relaxation on a Pacific beach, almost all your time here is devoted to nature excursions. Day five is reserved for departure or a transfer to another place for further relaxation, but an extended beach stay is not a required part of this itinerary.

## Why Tortuguero gets most of the time

[Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/) lies on the Caribbean side of Costa Rica. Its network of natural canals makes boats the main way to travel and observe the surrounding forest. On day two, the journey from San José passes through the humid forest area of [Braulio Carrillo](/costa-rica/place/braulio-carrillo-national-park/), then continues to the dock and by water to the lodge.

The itinerary includes a walk through Tortuguero village. The following day features a boat excursion along the national park canals and a walk on nature trails. Viewing wildlife in its natural habitat from the water is particularly rewarding: the scene changes around every bend, and sightings depend on the time of day, rainfall, and animal activity.

Sightings of specific wild animals cannot be guaranteed. Tortuguero is associated with sea turtles, but this tour describes boat and walking nature excursions rather than promising an encounter with nesting turtles. If you especially want seasonal turtle watching, arrange the appropriate dates and permitted visiting format separately.

## The advantages of staying overnight at a lodge

Two nights at Pachira Lodge Tortuguero let you head out onto the canals without making the return trip to the capital that same evening. The boat journey itself and staying amid the natural landscape are central to the experience. This is very different from a short day trip by road.

Pack a lightweight waterproof jacket, footwear suitable for wet trails, insect repellent, and waterproof protection for your phone or camera for the humid Caribbean zone. Remember that the itinerary includes a boat excursion and that wildlife observations depend on the weather. Heavy rain can affect both visibility and conditions on the water.

## Poás Volcano and La Paz Waterfall Gardens

On day four, a small aircraft operated by a local airline flies guests from Tortuguero to San José. **This flight is included in the tour price.** The land-based excursion then heads to [Poás Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/) and [La Paz Waterfalls](/costa-rica/place/la-paz-waterfalls/).

The volcanic crater is the main attraction at Poás. Weather at altitude differs considerably from the humid coast: it can be cool, cloudy, and windy. Views of the crater depend on visibility, and access to specific areas may be restricted during volcanic activity. Pack a light warm layer and a rain jacket in your daypack even after the hot Caribbean portion.

At La Paz Waterfall Gardens, forest trails lead past cascades. During the visit, you see enclosures and exhibits featuring birds, butterflies, reptiles, and other local fauna. This is another way to experience Costa Rican nature, compared with Tortuguero's canals: here the focus is walking through a managed attraction.

## Logistics of this short trip

A five-day itinerary leaves little free time. Day four is particularly busy: a domestic flight followed by the volcano and waterfalls. When selecting international flights, do not think of this tour as a collection of separate day trips from San José: it includes overnight stays in Tortuguero and a flight back.

Day five offers **two possible endings**: a transfer to your next beach destination or a return to the airport. Arrange the final transfer at the same time as your return flight. Adding a separate beach holiday changes the actual total length of your journey.

## What's included and what's extra

The price covers a **Russian-speaking guide**, transfers and excursions, accommodation, local hotel taxes, the domestic flight from Tortuguero to San José, and breakfast, lunch, and dinner on the days specified in the itinerary. The program lasts **5 days and 4 nights**.

Admission to Tortuguero National Park is charged separately at **$17 per person** under the published tour terms. Airport fees, personal expenses, and optional activities are not included either. Check the current park entry and ticketing rules before traveling, as these are set by the protected area's administration.

Compared with the [seven-day itinerary via Arenal and Tamarindo](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-short-complete-tour/), this tour focuses on Tortuguero and canal excursions. For more active routes, Monteverde, and the Pacific coast, consider the [nine-day “Beach and Mountains” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-beaches-mountains/).

## Frequently asked questions about the five-day trip

### Is the domestic flight from Tortuguero included?

Yes. The **Tortuguero–San José flight** is included in the price. It is one of the distinguishing features of the route's logistics.

### Are there beach days in the itinerary?

There are no mandatory beach days. On the last day you can choose a transfer to your next beach destination, but any additional nights by the sea are an extension of the trip.

### Are sea turtle sightings guaranteed?

No. The itinerary includes nature experiences and boat excursions in Tortuguero but promises neither a particular turtle sighting nor observations of nesting. Consider the season and local restrictions if this is your main interest.

### Do we pay extra for Tortuguero National Park?

Yes. The tour's “Not included” section specifies an entrance fee of **$17 per person**. Confirm current conditions before visiting.

### What language is the guide?

The tour includes a **Russian-speaking guide**. This distinguishes it from some other Costa Rica itineraries that provide English-speaking guidance.

## “5 Wonders of Costa Rica”: an active 9-day journey through volcanoes and cloud forests

The [“5 Wonders of Costa Rica” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-wonders/) is a **9-day, 8-night** itinerary beginning and ending in the [Liberia](/costa-rica/place/liberia/) area. It connects [Rincón de la Vieja](/costa-rica/place/rincon-de-la-vieja/), [Río Celeste](/costa-rica/place/rio-celeste/), [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), and the Pacific beaches.

The most important consideration when choosing this tour is your appetite for physical activity. It includes hiking routes, suspension bridges, horseback riding, canopy adventures, and travel through several natural regions. The final days by the ocean provide a break after a busy itinerary, although the beach portion is shorter than in [“3 Perspectives on Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-3-perspectives/).

## Rincón de la Vieja: an active start

After arriving through Liberia Airport, travelers head to [Rincón de la Vieja](/costa-rica/place/rincon-de-la-vieja/). Day two features a Mega Combo Tour: suspension bridges, a cable car, horseback riding, hot springs, and a waterfall. With so many experiences in one day, consider how comfortable you are with heights on aerial rope-course sections and with several activities in succession.

A canopy tour, a cable car, and a suspension bridge offer different ways of seeing the forest. Before particular activities, the operator may check age, height, weight, or health restrictions. Requirements should be confirmed for the specific site; being included in the itinerary does not remove the need for safety briefings and compliance with safety rules.

## Río Celeste: a forest trail and turquoise water

Day three is devoted to [Río Celeste](/costa-rica/place/rio-celeste/). The route follows humid tropical forest trails to a waterfall and Los Teñideros, the river section known for its unusual blue coloration. The water's appearance results from the optical properties of suspended particles, while the intensity of the color varies with light and river conditions.

The trail follows natural terrain and can become slippery after rain. Visits to Tenorio National Park are subject to restrictions on entry times and visitor numbers, and tickets are distributed through the park system's official service. Plan the Río Celeste visit around a designated time rather than treating it as an unrestricted stop between hotels.

## Maleku culture and Arenal: people and nature

Day four includes an introduction to the Maleku people's culture, including dance and handicrafts. The group then travels toward [Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/). This cultural stop adds context by offering a chance to learn about local traditions; it is not a promise of a carnival festival or entry to private community events.

The next day brings suspension bridges and walks in Arenal Volcano National Park. Visitors follow permitted trails among vegetation and traces of earlier volcanic activity. Climbing the volcanic cone itself is not part of standard tourist routes.

At Arenal and Rincón de la Vieja, closed-toe hiking boots, a rain jacket, drinking water, and clothing adaptable to changing conditions are useful. Trail conditions and access to particular areas depend on rainfall and current park authority instructions.

## Monteverde: the forest from another level

On day six, the journey crosses Lake Arenal by boat and continues toward [Monteverde and Santa Elena](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). A canopy adventure above the treetops is included in the cloud forest. Unlike walking on volcanic slopes, this experience focuses on the forest's upper canopy, moist air, and very different vegetation.

Brightly colored tropical birds, including quetzals, live around Monteverde, but sightings of particular species cannot be guaranteed on any given day. This tour will appeal to nature enthusiasts who value contrasting ecosystems and ways of observing wildlife, rather than simply collecting photos at viewpoints.

## Two beach days to finish

On day seven, the group reaches the [Pacific Ocean](/costa-rica/place/pacific-coast/). The following day is free, while day nine is devoted to the return transfer to Liberia Airport. After canopy activities, hikes, and several transfers, guests can relax by the sea.

| Region | Main activity |
|---|---|
| Rincón de la Vieja | Full day of varied activities |
| Río Celeste | Waterfall hike |
| Arenal | Bridges and volcanic trails |
| Monteverde | Cloud forest canopy tour |
| Pacific Ocean | Relaxation before departure |

## Included services and who this tour suits

The package includes accommodation in hotels along the route, transfers, scheduled excursions, the services of a Russian-speaking guide, and accommodation taxes. Meals are included as specified for the respective days. Optional activities, airport fees, and personal expenses are not included.

This itinerary is designed for travelers ready for several consecutive active days. If you have limited mobility, are uncomfortable with heights, or want more time by the water, consider a [more relaxed 10-day route](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-3-perspectives/). Other options are available in the [Costa Rica tour catalog](/costa-rica/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about “5 Wonders of Costa Rica”

### How much time is spent at the ocean?

The transfer to the coast is on day seven. Day eight is free, and day nine ends with the airport transfer.

### What is a canopy tour in Monteverde?

It is an activity on equipped elevated courses above the forest. The operator sets the exact participation and safety requirements.

### Will we climb to the top of Arenal?

No. The itinerary includes walks along designated national park trails, not an ascent of the volcano's cone.

### Is a Russian-speaking guide included?

Yes, a Russian-speaking guide is included in the tour price.
